thread.title: Technology Sector Update for 06/15/2018: OLED, JBL, QCOM, NXPI, FITB

author: MT Newswires
title: Technology Sector Update for 06/15/2018: OLED, JBL, QCOM, NXPI, FITB
text:
CSCO -1.16%
GOOG -0.16%
Technology stocks declined Friday, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 losing more than 0.4% in value today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a 0.1% decrease.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
- Universal Display ( OLED ) was almost 6% lower in late Friday trading following reports Apple ( AAPL ) may opt for less expensive versions of liquid crystal display screens in the next versions of its iPhone instead of the pricier organic-light-emitting-diode screens. Apple believes a large share of sales decision will be motivated by price concerns, according to the Wall Street Journal, and as a result will continue to produce devices with LCD screens this fall and continuing into 2019. Samsung is Apple's main OLED supplier but Universal Display shares often move in tandem with OLED news.
In other sector news:
- Qualcomm ( QCOM ) was swinging between small gains and losses Friday after the specialty chipmaker again extended the cash tender period for its proposed buyout of NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ) extends cash tender offer period by another week until next Thursday at 5 p.m. ET. Through the most recent deadline Thursday night, NXP investors had tendered slightly more than 16.3 million of their shares, representing about 4.7% of the rival chipmaker's outstanding stock, down from around 17.7 million shares tendered on June 7.
- Fitbit ( FIT ) slumped about 3% on Friday after six current and former employees of the wearable technology company were charged with stealing trade secrets from a now-defunct rival. The indictment filed Thursday by the U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of California in San Jose accuses the Fitbit employees of receiving trade secrets from Jawbone without authorization after leaving the company. Jawbone previously also accused Fitbit of a 2015 clandestine effort to steal talent, trade secrets and intellectual property before agreeing to a December settlement.
- Jabil Circuit (JBL) retreated Friday, sliding as much as 10%, despite the contract manufacturer reporting fiscal Q3 financial results exceeding Wall Street estimates. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $0.46 per share compared with a $0.31 per share non-GAAP profit during the same quarter last year and topping the Capital IQ consensus by $0.02 per share. Revenue rose to $5.44 billion from $4.49 billion during the year-ago period, also easily surpassing the $4.90 billion Street view. Jabil also is projecting adjusted Q4 net income in a range of $0.56 to $0.80 per share on $5.2 billion to $5.6 billion in revenue, straddling the analyst means expecting a non-GAAP profit of $0.68 per share on $5.2 billion in revenue. It also authorized the repurchase of up to $350 million of its shares through Aug. 31, 2019.
